experiment: IQLD x SAC-prior self-bootstrap on 'hard' scenes - resumed from offline_hard best_safe (0.51)
mechanism: Warm start from IQLD offline checkpoint; frozen copy of the deterministic IQLD actor becomes pi_prior; critics switch to SAC-style TD target at the current policy's own next-state actions (target-Q polyak); policy loss = anchor(adv-weighted BC to expert data) + prior_weight(t)*E||pi_theta(s)-pi_prior(s)||^2 (frozen-prior trust region, annealed 3.0->0.6) + sac_weight*(alpha*log pi - min Q(s,a~pi)); symmetric 50/50 online/offline batches; eval uses deterministic mean actions.
conclusion: Prior-anchored SAC lifts IQLD on hard scenes from ~0.5 to teacher level in 150ep (fixed beta: robust 0.764-0.784 > teacher 0.714) and BEYOND with annealed prior release at 300ep: latest robust 0.842 vs teacher 0.714 (z=4.87, p<1e-5); nominal 0.79-0.81 vs teacher 0.834 (below, NS). NOTE: seed-11 25-ep validation under-estimates this family badly (0.28@300 vs formal robust 0.842) - trust multi-seed formal. Annealed release materially helps robust.
